title: perf-canary: add compaction-enabled KV cache fragmentation scenario + gating on p99 and alloc-failure rate
author: Rina Kobayashi
release_notes:
- Add a new perf-canary scenario that runs bursty mixed-length traffic with KV compaction enabled and gates on p99 latency + allocator failure metrics
- Export canary artifacts/metrics tags to make compaction regressions diagnosable by pool/model family
body:
Title: Add perf-canary check for compaction-enabled runtime (gating on p99 + allocator failures)

Context
We’re rolling out the KV cache compaction work behind a runtime flag. The main remaining risk is tail regression from (a) compaction overhead/sync points and (b) allocator churn (allocation failures / emergency eviction) under bursty traffic and mixed sequence length distributions.

This PR adds a dedicated perf-canary scenario that:
- Runs the runtime with compaction enabled (feature flag + budgets)
- Exercises bursty arrivals with mixed context lengths (prefill/decode interleaving)
- Gates releases on p99 latency and allocator failure rate

This is intended to catch “looks fine on average, but p99 blows up” issues before we canary broadly, and to provide a stable signal for tuning compaction trigger thresholds/budgets.

What changed (high-level)
- New canary scenario: kv_compaction_bursty_mix
  - Arrival pattern: burst windows (60s) + idle windows (120s)
  - Prompt distribution: mixed short/medium/long contexts; long-context requests are capped to avoid unrealistic OOM-only behavior while still stressing fragmentation
  - Multi-tenant mix: two “tenants” with different weights; tags emitted for tenant tier to ensure no single tenant is masking the regression
- Runtime config wiring for compaction
  - Enables compaction via runtime flag in the canary harness
  - Sets conservative initial budget defaults (time budget per interval + max bytes moved) aligned with the design doc assumptions
- New gating rules
  - p99 latency gate: scenario p99 must not regress > 7% vs last-green baseline (rolling baseline pinned per GPU class)
  - allocator failure gate: kv_cache_alloc_failures_total must be <= 1e-6 per generated token (normalized) and absolute failures <= 2 / run
  - stability gate: ignore the first warmup interval; require 2 consecutive measurement intervals under thresholds to avoid flake
- Better artifact capture
  - Captures allocator/fragmentation counters as a structured metrics blob alongside the latency histogram
  - Annotates runs with runtime build SHA + compaction config used (budgets/thresholds)

Why these thresholds
- p99 regression threshold chosen to be strict enough to catch sync-point regressions but tolerant of minor noise across regions/GPU types.
- allocator failure threshold chosen because we saw “rare but deadly” allocator failures correlate strongly with timeouts (SUP-4410) and OOM churn (SUP-4422). Even a small uptick is meaningful.

Implementation notes
- We normalize allocator failures per generated token because absolute request counts differ when throughput shifts slightly; this makes the gate robust.
- The scenario uses the same model family as our existing burst tail scenario to avoid introducing confounds.
- This PR does not change any production defaults; it only changes perf-canary gating and artifacts.

Related
- Runtime series (redwood repo): compaction engine + scheduler integration + feature flag plumbing
- Linear: ENG-2854 (perf-canary), ENG-2851 (canary plan)

Checklist
- [x] Scenario definition added and validated locally
- [x] Baseline run created and pinned (per GPU class)
- [x] Gates run on CI and are non-flaky across 10 consecutive runs
- [x] Artifact export includes compaction config + runtime SHA

Commits
1) canary/scenarios: add kv_compaction_bursty_mix scenario definition
2) harness/runtime: allow passing through compaction flags + budgets
3) gating: add p99 + alloc failure gates with warmup handling
4) artifacts: export allocator counters + config metadata
5) docs: update perf-canary README with new scenario and interpretation notes

Changed files (summary)
- scenarios/kv_compaction_bursty_mix.yaml
- harness/runtime_flags.py
- gating/rules/latency.py
- gating/rules/allocator.py (new)
- metrics/exporter.py
- baselines/pinned_baselines.json
- docs/scenarios.md

CI / Checks
- unit-tests: PASS
- scenario-lint: PASS
- baseline-compare (A100): PASS
- baseline-compare (H100): PASS
- flake-check (10x rerun): PASS

Review conversation (selected)
Marcus Reed: “Can we avoid a single p99 threshold across all hardware? We’ve seen p99 noise differ between A100/H100.”
Rina Kobayashi: “Agreed. Implemented baseline pinning per GPU class and gated on relative regression vs last-green per class. Added warmup + consecutive-interval requirement to reduce flake.”

Kira Volkov: “Allocator failures absolute <=2/run feels arbitrary. Why not strictly 0?”
Rina Kobayashi: “We do see rare single failures in noisy lab conditions even without compaction (driver hiccups). The normalized per-token threshold is the primary gate; the absolute gate is a sanity check to prevent a ‘small per-token’ pass when throughput craters. Added note to docs and linked SUP tickets.”

Allison Grant: “Please ensure metrics names align with the telemetry schema we’re standardizing (kv_cache_alloc_failures_total vs alloc_failures).”
Rina Kobayashi: “Updated to kv_cache_alloc_failures_total and kv_cache_compaction_bytes_moved_total, plus tags (region, pool, model_family) so dashboards can join canary artifacts with prod metrics.”

Rafael Mendes: “For oncall, what’s the action when this gate trips? Is it always rollback?”
Rina Kobayashi: “Added docs section ‘When gate trips’ with decision tree: if alloc failures spike -> disable compaction flag in release candidate / tune budgets; if only p99 regresses -> inspect compaction time + stream sync counters; in both cases block release until a runtime fix or config change is validated.”

Outcome
Merged via squash. This will run on the runtime release train starting next scheduled canary window. Baselines are pinned and will be updated only via explicit baseline-update PRs.
